short: Lennart Torstensson annihilated an Imperial army near Leipzig, cementing Swedish control over Saxony.
full:
On 23 October 1642, the Swedish army under Field Marshal Lennart Torstensson encountered an Imperial force commanded by Archduke Leopold Wilhelm and Ottavio Piccolomini on the same ground where Gustavus Adolphus had won his famous victory eleven years earlier. The Swedes, attempting to lift the siege of Leipzig, aggressively attacked the Imperial positions.

A devastating Swedish cavalry charge on the left wing quickly shattered the Imperial right, leading to a general collapse of the Habsburg lines. The Imperial army suffered enormous casualties and lost its entire artillery train. The decisive victory cemented Swedish dominance over Saxony, forced the Emperor to reconsider peace, and demonstrated Torstensson's brilliance as a commander.
